videos.script: When are Horta's customers ordering? Here is a table. Seven days, fifteen hours, one hundred and five numbers. {{table}} Nobody reads a hundred and five numbers. So keep the table, and replace every number with a shade. The more orders, the stronger the colour. {{shade}} Now a pattern appears at once. On weekdays, a strong band at seven in the evening. At the weekend, the strongest cells move to the late morning. {{pattern}} That is a heatmap. It is a table where colour does the first reading, and it works whenever both the rows and the columns are categories or steps. {{heatmap}} The same idea shows how several variables move together. A correlation matrix colours each pair by how strongly they are related. {{matrix}} In this lesson you build both. And you learn the two choices that decide whether anyone can read them: the order of the rows, and whether the numbers stay in the cells. {{plan}}
